areas.name: Magma reservoirs and large eruptions
areas.blurb: How silicic magma bodies are assembled, stored and remobilised before eruption, read from the age and chemistry of zircon and other accessory minerals — from the Yellowstone–Snake River Plain and the Kneeling Nun Tuff to Toba, Lipari and the Pannonian Basin.

areas.name: High-precision U–Pb geochronology
areas.blurb: Developing and testing ID-TIMS methods — new amplifier technology, microsampling, chemical abrasion, interlaboratory reproducibility and community reporting standards — so that dates are precise, accurate and comparable between laboratories.

areas.name: Reference materials and in situ dating
areas.blurb: Characterising reference materials for in situ dating and thermometry, including synthetic and natural calcite for carbonate U–Pb geochronology, zircon standards and tin–tungsten minerals.

areas.name: Large igneous provinces and Earth history
areas.blurb: Dating flood basalt provinces and their silicic counterparts — Deccan, Karoo, Columbia River, Paraná-Etendeka and the Atlantic magmatic provinces — and providing time constraints for climate, biological and tectonic events.

areas.name: Ore deposits and critical metals
areas.blurb: Timescales of magmatic-hydrothermal systems that form porphyry copper and tin deposits, and the behaviour of lithium in volcanic rocks as a source for brine deposits.

areas.name: Lunar and planetary chronology
areas.blurb: High-precision dating of Apollo zircons to constrain the solidification of the lunar magma ocean and major impact events on the early Moon.
